Answer: C
Reason: The CT images demonstrate massive dilation of the central airways (trachea and main bronchi) alongside multiple large cystic spaces, which is characteristic of tracheobronchomegaly (Mounier-Kuhn syndrome). The "cavities" seen on the chest X-ray correspond to these dilated bronchi, and the right hilar opacity represents the enlarged, fluid-filled or mucus-filled bronchus intermedius.
